Input image 1 is the edit target and continuity reference: preserve its one cropped female traveler, feminine white/deep-violet/gold pleated dress, opaque white legwear and deep-violet butterfly-trim ankle boots, the ordinary white city bicycle with real wear, original quiet forest asphalt lane and daylight. Input image 2 is ONLY the original Vivhite sticker artwork reference; retain its exact fixed open violet-pink star irises and thin gold round glasses as a small inert decal on the existing diagonal frame tube.
Primary repair: establish a mechanically correct bicycle AND a visibly supported seated rider. Recompose slightly wider as a level drive-side view of her LOWER WAIST through both boots, with her entire chest, neck and head safely above the upper image boundary. Show a real BLACK PADDED BICYCLE SADDLE directly under her seated hips. Its rear edge and the forward projecting saddle nose must both be plainly identifiable outside the hem, not hidden completely by her skirt. Show the short exposed metal seatpost and its clamp mechanically and continuously joining the saddle rails to the actual bicycle seat tube above the rear wheel, with correct support, perspective, scale and shadows. Her modest skirt rests naturally over her seated hips; no floating pelvis and no standing on pedals. Leave clear negative space beside the seatpost so its connection is readable. Keep the saddle and seatpost well within the picture, not clipped by the top/left edge. Keep the normal bicycle geometry: two wheels in one plane, fork attached to front hub, seat tube leading to crank bottom bracket, rear stays connected to rear hub, two opposed crank arms 180 degrees apart, one flat pedal beneath each boot, coherent chain running from the front chainring to the rear sprocket. Her two knees have a natural complementary pedaling pose and her feet rest securely on those opposite pedals.
Photorealistic ordinary travel snapshot with restrained natural color, believable fabric, leather, metal, road grit and forest light; do not glamorize or add fantasy effects. This is a rider-and-bicycle mechanics correction, not a pinup. Preserve modest feminine travel styling and existing merchandise identity. No other person, no face or head or chin or portrait reflection, no extra limbs, no separate hands, no third leg, no extra bike, no readable lettering, no captions, no watermark. The only drawn face is the fixed sticker. Make the visible black saddle and unbroken attached seatpost unambiguous.
